onlineOffline.q: What is the difference between the online and offline course?
onlineOffline.a: Both follow the same syllabus and tests. Offline adds classroom teaching, daily physical training on our ground, the library and a hostel option. Online lets you attend live from home and watch recordings.

demo.q: Can I attend a class before paying?
demo.a: Yes. Book a free live class from this page and sit in a real class from this batch.

material.a: Yes. You get printed notes for offline students and PDF notes for online students, plus mock tests based on the latest exam pattern.

physical.a: Offline students train daily on our ground with ex-service trainers. Online students get a training plan and video guidance.

hostel.a: Yes, there is a hostel and mess near the academy for offline students. It is not included in the course fee and is charged separately; ask our counsellor about seats and charges.

fees.q: Can I pay the fee in parts?
fees.a: Yes, instalment options are available. Our counsellor will explain the plan when you book your seat.

support.q: Whom do I contact if I have a problem?
support.a: Message us on WhatsApp or request a callback from this page. Our team replies the same day.

agniveer-6-month-plan.title: How to crack Agniveer GD in 6 months: a month-by-month plan
agniveer-6-month-plan.excerpt: A simple plan that splits your six months between the written exam, the physical test and revision.
agniveer-6-month-plan.p1: Agniveer GD has three hurdles: the written exam, the physical fitness test and the medical. Most students lose out because they prepare for only one of them. From day one, split every day into a study block and a ground block.
agniveer-6-month-plan.p2: In months one and two, finish the GK and maths basics and build your running base with easy 3 km runs. In months three and four, take two mock tests a week and work on your 1.6 km time. In months five and six, revise only from your own notes and your mock-test mistakes.
agniveer-6-month-plan.p3: Sleep seven hours, eat simple food and record your run times in a notebook. Consistency beats intensity: a steady plan for six months is better than a hard push for six weeks.

police-run-tips.title: Police physical test: tips to clear the long-distance run
police-run-tips.excerpt: Pacing, shoes, breathing and the weekly schedule our PT instructors use with every batch.
police-run-tips.p1: The run in a police physical test must be finished within the time set in the official notification, so read it first and work out the pace per kilometre you need. Start a little slower than that pace and speed up only in the last kilometre.
police-run-tips.p2: Train four days a week: one long slow run, one interval session (400 m repeats), one hill or stair session and one easy recovery run. Add skipping and squats twice a week for leg strength.
police-run-tips.p3: Run in light, well-fitting shoes you have already trained in. Never try new shoes, new food or a new route in the week before the test. Breathe in a steady rhythm and keep your shoulders relaxed.

ssc-gd-2026.title: SSC GD Constable: posts, eligibility and how to apply
ssc-gd-2026.excerpt: What a 10th-pass student needs to know before filling the SSC GD Constable form.
ssc-gd-2026.p1: SSC GD Constable recruits for central armed police forces such as BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP and SSB. Candidates who have passed 10th and are within the age limit can apply online on the SSC website.
ssc-gd-2026.p2: Selection has several stages: a computer-based test, a physical efficiency test, a physical standard test and a medical examination. The written test covers reasoning, general knowledge, maths and Hindi or English.
ssc-gd-2026.p3: Keep your documents ready before you apply: 10th marksheet, photo, signature and caste or NCC certificate if any. Always confirm dates and vacancies on the official SSC notice; figures on our site are indicative.

nda-maths-strategy.title: NDA maths: the chapters to start with
nda-maths-strategy.excerpt: Where to spend your time first if you have only three months for the NDA maths paper.
nda-maths-strategy.p1: The NDA maths paper has negative marking, so speed and accuracy matter more than covering every chapter.
nda-maths-strategy.p2: Algebra, trigonometry, calculus and matrices usually carry the most questions. Start with these, then move to coordinate geometry, statistics and probability.
nda-maths-strategy.p3: Solve at least five previous-year papers in exam timing. Mark every question you got wrong and redo it a week later. Our NDA batch runs a timed maths test every Sunday.

budget-diet-plan.title: A simple, budget diet plan for defence aspirants
budget-diet-plan.excerpt: Home-cooked meals that give you energy for morning runs without costly supplements.
budget-diet-plan.p1: You do not need protein powders to clear a physical test. Dal, chana, eggs, milk, curd, seasonal fruit and rotis give most students the protein and energy they need.
budget-diet-plan.p2: Eat a light snack such as a banana or soaked chana 30 minutes before a morning run, and a full breakfast after it. Drink water through the day, not only after training.
budget-diet-plan.p3: Cut down on fried snacks, cold drinks and late-night meals. Sleep is part of your diet: without seven hours of sleep your body cannot recover from training.

success-rohit.title: From a village in Etawah to Agniveer: Rohit’s story
success-rohit.excerpt: How a farmer’s son balanced farm work, study and running, and cleared Agniveer GD in his first attempt.
success-rohit.p1: Rohit Yadav joined our offline batch after 10th, with no coaching background and a slow 1.6 km time. He helped on the family farm every morning before class.
success-rohit.p2: He followed the batch plan strictly: ground training at 5 AM, classes till noon and self-study in the library till evening. In four months his run time improved by more than two minutes.
success-rohit.p3: He cleared Agniveer GD in his first attempt. His advice to new students: write your daily targets on paper and do not skip the ground even on rainy days.
